fields.v: Hong, D., Chi, Y., Li, W., Wang, X., Gao, M., Yang, K., He, B., Zheng, Y., Xiao, C., Na, Q. (2026). SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration? arXiv:2608.23564v1 [cs.CL], 24 Aug 2026. Homepage https://lab.einsia.ai/swe-refactor-bench
Preprint — arXiv:2608.23564v1 [cs.CL]; no published venue stated
Navers Lab, Einsia.AI (industry) and Tsinghua University (per-author mapping not given)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — SWE Refactor Bench, 20 whole-repository stack migrations with a three-stage protocol (Migration Audit by LLM judge as veto, Behavioural Tests with 130,118 fixed checks, Agentic Verification by six coding agents generating differential counterexamples); 8 models in 26 model-effort configurations compared

No SDD approach. Configurations: Claude Code harness with claude-opus-5 (low/medium/high/xhigh/max), claude-sonnet-5 (5 efforts), kimi-k3 (max), qwen3.8-max (max), dsv4-flash (max), glm-5.2 (max); Codex harness with gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-luna (none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max). Harness versions not stated

Benchmark task artefacts: State A repository archive, State B declaration naming the target stack and versions, instruction I (requirements in full, no behavioural checks), offline image with both toolchains, artifact contract; hidden: migration criteria (prompt questions), recorded Stage II expectations, verifier allow/deny lists

Agent works autonomously: understand repository and requirements, plan, rewrite onto target stack, build and debug, verify against State A; then hidden evaluation: Stage I Migration Audit (veto), Stage II Behavioural Tests (all-or-nothing), Stage III Agentic Verification (six verifiers, one hour each)
None in the agent workflow (autonomous, no network beyond model endpoint). Two SE researchers annotated 156 runs to validate the Stage I judge
N/A (no SDD approach); full autonomous agent runs (6-30 h budget per task)
Not classifiable (benchmark of coding agents; no SDD terms used by the authors)
Existing code base (whole-repository migration of a working repository to another language, framework, platform or build toolchain, behaviour preserved)

20 tasks from 20 upstream projects, 867,062 source LoC in total (per task 0.8k-358k LoC; language tasks 4.4k-39.8k), 10,594 version-controlled files; 136 migration criteria (Stage I), 264 test modules and 130,118 behavioural checks (Stage II; more than 6,000 per task on average); time budget 6-30 h per task (262 h in total)

rev.why: Totals row of Tables 1 and 10 is 262 (budget hours), 136 (criteria), 264 (modules): per-task criteria sum to 136 (e.g. lang01 has 8) and 3,536 criterion verdicts = 136 x 26 (p. 12). The draft gave 262 criteria and 136 modules.

Migration completeness via Stage I criteria (old stack absent from repository and build closure, target stack is the real implementation, no shims or embedded reference)

Verifier break rate, exclusive breaks, time to counterexample (median 17.0 min); judge agreement (unanimity rate, judge vs human kappa)

Automatic: Stage I by LLM judge gpt-5.6-sol answering each criterion three times with majority vote and cited evidence; Stage II fixed checks recorded from a reference build of State A in a separate image; Stage III six coding-agent verifiers (claude-opus-5 x2, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, claude-sonnet-5) must submit an executable counterexample that passes on State A, fails on the submission and reproduces three times. Manual: two SE researchers judged 156 runs blind to the judge

No success criterion stated by the authors for a configuration (quality and cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors). One run per task (20 runs each); behavioural pass % / score / USD per task: Claude Code + claude-opus-5 low 92.5/20.5/34.8, medium 92.7/28.5/38.4, high 92.8/34.5/55.7, xhigh 92.8/47.0/74.9 (best, 5 accepted of 20), max 91.9/31.0/72.4; Codex + gpt-5.6-sol none 63.6/4.0/2.9, low 62.0/7.0/5.9, medium 70.8/6.5/6.0, high 74.0/19.0/7.7, xhigh 73.5/9.5/19.1, max 84.1/28.5/143.5; Claude Code + kimi-k3 max 93.9/19.5/28.9; Claude Code + claude-sonnet-5 low 79.2/4.0/4.4, medium 73.9/15.0/11.9, high 85.6/6.0/24.6, xhigh 76.5/9.0/27.0, max 84.3/8.5/27.5; Codex + gpt-5.6-luna none 66.4/4.0/1.6, low 58.3/4.0/1.7, medium 66.6/0.0/1.7, high 75.6/4.0/1.8, xhigh 83.8/5.5/2.9, max 89.1/10.5/2.8 (no acceptances); Claude Code + qwen3.8-max max 74.7/10.0/14.5; Claude Code + dsv4-flash max 90.7/7.0/4.3 (no acceptances); Claude Code + glm-5.2 max 85.2/6.5/17.5 (no acceptances)

Tasks: 20 migrations. Configurations: 8 models x effort levels = 26 (GPT-series under Codex, others under Claude Code). Held constant: task image, instruction, time budget per task, offline container (network only to model endpoint), hidden three-stage evaluation. Baseline: none (empty-diff submission discussed analytically as the blindness case). Acceptance tests: Stage I criteria, Stage II fixed checks, Stage III executable counterexamples. Repetitions: one run per configuration per task (520 runs). Human intervention: none

Only 28 of 520 runs (5.4%) accepted; 13 of 20 tasks never solved; best claude-opus-5 xhigh 47.0/100, then gpt-5.6-sol 28.5, kimi-k3 19.5, claude-sonnet-5 15.0; gpt-5.6-luna, dsv4-flash and glm-5.2 no acceptances. 30 runs blindness (behaviour kept without migrating), 252 migrated but broke behaviour; of 340 migrated runs 58% reach 99% of checks, 26% reach 100%; of 88 reaching Stage III, 60 (68.2%) broken by verifiers. By class: build toolchain 31.4, platform 17.2, framework 12.0, language 5.6. No significance tests

Yes per authors: three stages stop disjoint sets of submissions; Stage I judge 96.3% unanimous across three samples, 89.7% agreement with humans (kappa 0.795), errors mostly too strict; no self-preference found for judge or verifiers. Limits stated: results depend on the verifier panel (without the two opus verifiers 46 instead of 28 accepted); acceptance is survival against the strongest adversaries, not proof of correctness; results do not rank intrinsic difficulty of all migrations

No limitations section. Stated limits: capability gap shown only on these 20 tasks; accepted migration is not proven correct; scores depend on verifier panel strength; formal verification not feasible for cross-language whole-repository rewrites. Gap: agents cannot reliably complete migrations that are complete, behaviour-preserving and robust to adversarial verification; behaviour-only benchmarks suffer from 'Blindness'

Values from Tables 2-6, 9-10 and text (table layout jumbled by extraction; Table 3 rows rebuilt in caption order, consistent with text: opus 47.0, sol 28.5, kimi 19.5, sonnet 15.0; Table 1/10 totals rebuilt and checked against per-task rows and the 3,536 criterion verdicts). Reporting points: human validation by 'two software-engineering researchers ... 156 runs of 6 tasks ..., three tasks each' (apparently one researcher per three tasks, so no inter-annotator agreement is reported); the Stage I judge (gpt-5.6-sol) and five of the six verifiers (claude-opus-5 x2, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-luna, claude-sonnet-5) use models that are also evaluated (self-preference checked, p. 12, 14). Data availability: homepage only; release of tasks and harness not stated. No pre-registration. Programming languages: C, C++, C#, Rust, Java, Go, Zig, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python (State A/B pairs)

rev.why: The draft said two verifier models are also evaluated systems, but four evaluated models supply five of the six verifiers (Fig. 6); the 'three tasks each' wording points to a split of tasks between the two annotators rather than an unexplained combination.
